title: Freshness checks
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for finding stale, deprecated or end-of-life knowledge: watch items, a deterministic freshness policy, deprecation notices, tombstones and a daily scan proposal that is not activated.
boundaries: Read only public release notes, deprecation pages and package indexes. Do not sign up, log in, file reports or contact anyone.
No scheduler is activated; the daily scan is a proposal noun.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for finding stale, deprecated or end-of-life knowledge

value.lets_workers: Keep the nouns other packs rely on from quietly going out of date: watch the tools, packages, APIs, models and pages they pin, flag what is stale, deprecated or out of support, propose refreshes and replacements, and record do-not-use tombstones with evidence.

flow.when: Daily, from the schedule proposal; deterministic.
For watched items that are due or flagged.
For deprecated items with a named replacement; it proposes trials as follow-up verbs.
For end-of-life or unsafe versions, with evidence.

nouns.title: Freshness policy: max ages, flags and actions
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic rule set: the same watch items and date give the same flags and actions.

flags.older_than_max_age: Not checked within its max age.
flags.newer_upstream_version: Upstream released a newer version than the pinned one.
flags.deprecated_upstream: Upstream marked the pinned version or feature deprecated.
flags.end_of_life: Upstream ended support for the pinned version.
flags.license_changed: The upstream license differs from the one recorded.
flags.source_unreachable: The upstream source failed on two checks in a row.

actions.refresh: Re-read and write a superseding noun: older_than_max_age or newer_upstream_version.
actions.replace: Propose a replacement trial: deprecated_upstream with a named replacement.
actions.tombstone: Record a do-not-use tombstone: end_of_life, or a security advisory for the pinned version.
actions.ask_owner: license_changed or source_unreachable: a person decides.

value.rule: A 404 or timeout is not proof of deprecation; it is source_unreachable until confirmed.
value.starting_point: When an item has no max age, start from its category's default half-life in the registry.

nouns.title: Template: one thing to keep fresh: the noun that relies on it, its upstream identity, pinned version and how to check it

value.describes: one thing to keep fresh: the noun that relies on it, its upstream identity, pinned version and how to check it
rules: One watch item per upstream identity and pinned version.

nouns.category_reason: A watch item is a falsifiable assumption that a pinned version is still current.

nouns.title: Template: an upstream deprecation or end-of-life notice with its source and date

value.describes: an upstream deprecation or end-of-life notice with its source and date
rules: Quote what upstream says; do not infer deprecation from silence or a failed request.

nouns.category_reason: A notice is a dated snapshot of a public source.

nouns.title: Template: flags and actions for every watched item as of one date

value.describes: flags and actions for every watched item as of one date
rules: Flags and actions follow the freshness policy only.

nouns.category_reason: A freshness report is a deterministic check run.

nouns.title: Template: a do-not-use record for one version, with evidence and the replacement

value.describes: a do-not-use record for one version, with evidence and the replacement
rules: Evidence cites the upstream notice or advisory.
A replacement is named, or none with the reason.

nouns.category_reason: A tombstone is a verified negative record that prevents repeating a known failure.

nouns.title: Proposed daily freshness scan (not activated)
nouns.category_reason: A schedule proposal is stored as a seed hypothesis, following the research seed precedent.

value.activation_path: Recurring execution needs Tessera's flag-gated schedule support, which is being designed now. No scheduler is activated by this pack, and a schedule noun cannot authorize work by itself.

cadence.start_reason: Set by the owner when an authorized schedule adapter exists.

value.enqueue_identity: SHA-256 of the schedule key, its version and the window start, so duplicate ticks never create duplicate tasks.
value.missed_windows: Skip missed windows; never catch up more than one window.
value.follow_up: scan-staleness proposes check-deprecations, refresh and replacement verbs for flagged items; an authorized requester enqueues those.

verbs.title: Scan watched items for staleness
verbs.summary: Apply the freshness policy to every watched item as of one date, using recorded check results, and propose the follow-up verbs each flag calls for.
verbs.outcome: A freshness report with proposed follow-up verbs, or no_change when everything is current.

as_of.description: The date ages are measured from.

steps: Verify the pins. Compute flags and actions from the policy only; no network is needed for this verb.
Propose one check-deprecations verb for items that are due, and a propose-replacements or record-tombstone verb where the policy says so.
A failed request is source_unreachable, never deprecation.

acceptance.check: The report validates against template.freshness-report's schema.
Every pinned watch item appears exactly once.
Every action matches the policy's action for its flags.

verbs.title: Check upstream for deprecations
verbs.summary: Read the release feeds and deprecation pages of due watch items and record any deprecation or end-of-life notice with its source and date.
verbs.outcome: Deprecation notices and updated watch items, or no_change when nothing changed upstream.

slots.name: watch_items
slots.description: Pins of the due watch items.

steps: Verify the pins. Read only each item's release feed and deprecation page, within max_fetches.
Quote what upstream says and record the page's digest and date.
Write a superseding watch item with the new last_checked date and any newer upstream version.
Propose a record-tombstone verb for end-of-life notices and a propose-replacements verb for deprecations that name a replacement.
Read only public release notes, deprecation pages and package indexes. Do not sign up, log in, file reports or contact anyone.

acceptance.check: Notices and watch items validate against their templates.
Every notice's what field is supported by its source page.
Pages read are at most max_fetches.

network: Read-only requests to the watched items' release feeds and deprecation pages, at most max_fetches.

verbs.title: Propose replacements
verbs.summary: For each deprecated item with a named replacement, describe the replacement as a candidate and propose a comparable trial as a follow-up verb.
verbs.outcome: Proposed follow-up verbs and nouns, or no_change when no replacement is named.

slots.name: profile
slots.description: Pin of the project and hardware profile.

steps: Verify the pins. Write one candidate card per named replacement, with its license read at a pinned revision.
Propose a tool-discovery run-trial verb for each candidate worth trialing, with the pins it needs.
Read only public release notes, deprecation pages and package indexes. Do not sign up, log in, file reports or contact anyone.

acceptance.check: Every card validates against the tool-candidate template.
Every candidate worth trialing has a proposed run-trial verb.
Each replacement plausibly fits the profile.

network: Read-only requests to the replacements' upstream pages.

verbs.title: Record a do-not-use tombstone
verbs.summary: Check the evidence that a version is end of life or unsafe and record a tombstone that stops workers from using it again.
verbs.outcome: A tombstone, or no_change when the evidence does not support one.

slots.name: notice
slots.description: Pin of the deprecation, end-of-life or advisory notice.

slots.name: watch_item
slots.description: Pin of the affected watch item.

steps: Verify the pins and reread the notice's evidence.
Record a tombstone only when the notice clearly covers the pinned version.
Name the replacement, or say none with the reason.

acceptance.check: The tombstone validates against template.tombstone's schema.
Every evidence entry cites the notice or an advisory.
The notice covers the tombstoned version.
